title: Sum Root to Leaf Numbers
statement_short: Given the root of a binary tree containing digits from 0 to 9 only, each root-to-leaf path represents a number. Return the total sum of all root-to-leaf numbers.
constraints: 1 <= number of nodes in tree <= 1000, 0 <= Node.val <= 9, depth of tree will not exceed 10
hint: Tree depth <= 10 and node count <= 1000 permit recursive digit accumulation (current \* 10 + val) in O(n) time.
keywords: total sum of all root-to-leaf numbers
why_not: Right: Tree DFS passes running path values (val \* 10 + node.val) down to leaf nodes and sums them in O(n) time and O(h) space. Not Tree BFS: Level-order queue traversal accumulates numbers per node in O(n) time, but requires extra queue space for node-value pairs. Not Math / Geometry: Digit shifting uses base-10 math, but the traversal backbone is tree recursion. Not Backtracking: Explicitly building and converting string digit lists adds unnecessary allocation overhead.
